children: The Pennsylvania Department of Health is requesting emergency help from the CDC to contend with an ongoing measles outbreak on the condition that the agency recognizes four measles-associated deaths in the state.

A letter sent to CDC Director Erica Schwartz from Pennsylvania Secretary of Health Debra Bogen Wednesday evening asked for Epi-Aid, which "enables rapid response by CDC's Epidemic Intelligence Service ("EIS") officers in investigating urgent public health problems, such as infectious and noninfectious disease outbreaks, unexplained illnesses, or natural or manmade disasters," according to the agency.

"The CDC's choice not to publicly recognize the deaths undermines our response," Bogen said in the letter, reviewed by

. "For this reason, if CDC is unable to transparently and accurately communicate information about those measles-associated deaths, ​the Department will respectfully rescind our request for a CDC Epi-Aid."
As of Wednesday, the Pennsylvania DOH has reported 731 cases and 141 hospitalizations due to measles. Of the total cases, only four were in those who have not received the MMR vaccine.
